patients.summary: Retired math teacher with a 2013 mechanical mitral valve on warfarin, hypertension, type 2 diabetes, CKD 3a and hyperlipidemia who joins in 2022 just before a right hip replacement. The hip later becomes chronically infected and is treated with a two-stage exchange; severe aortic stenosis, tap-responsive normal pressure hydrocephalus (shunted) and recurrent bleeding from cecal angiodysplasia with iron deficiency follow. Today a capsule endoscopy is booked and the aortic stenosis has never been taken to intervention.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
New patient, 72 y/o retired HS math teacher, transferring care from a practice he'd been with for years. Main reason for coming: wants one doctor who will run his warfarin and see the whole picture.

HPI: Mechanical mitral valve placed in 2013. Has been on warfarin since, goal INR 2.5-3.5, on 5 mg nightly with occasional adjustments; last INRs at his old office in range per his log book, no bleeding or clot history he knows of. Also takes aspirin 81. HTN on lisinopril 20 and amlodipine 5, home readings he says are 'in the 120s.' DM2 for about ten years on metformin 1000 BID, last A1c 'just under 7.' Statin for lipids. Told his kidneys are 'stage 3, stable' for a few years. Constipation is long-standing, uses an OTC stool softener every so often, not bothersome. Colonoscopy spring 2021 with polyps removed, told 3 years.

Right hip: years of worsening pain, severe arthritis on x-ray per his surgeon, now limping and using the banister on stairs. Right total hip is booked for 9/27. He'll need a bridging plan for the warfarin, which is part of why he wanted to get established now.

PMH/PSH: as above. Mechanical MVR 2013. Polypectomy 2021.
Meds: warfarin 5 mg qhs, lisinopril 20 daily, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40 daily, amlodipine 5 daily, ASA 81 daily, docusate prn.
Allergies: NKDA.
Family hx: no colon cancer in the family, no early heart disease, nobody with HHT that he knows of.
Social: retired from teaching high school math. Quit smoking 2007, about 20 pack-years before that. Wine 1-2 glasses a week. Walks less than he'd like because of the hip.

ROS: neg for chest pain, palpitations, syncope, bleeding, black stools, urinary sx. Hip as above.

Exam: Well-appearing, pleasant. Vitals reviewed. HEENT unremarkable. Neck supple, no JVD. Heart: regular rhythm, crisp mechanical valve click. Lungs clear. Abd soft, NT, no masses. Ext no edema. Right hip with painful, limited internal rotation; antalgic gait. Feet: intact sensation to monofilament, pulses palpable, no lesions.

PHQ-2 negative.

A/P:
1. Mechanical mitral valve on warfarin - we'll take over INR management. INR today. Continue 5 mg nightly. ASA 81 continued.
2. Right hip OA, THA 9/27 - preop visit ~2 wks before surgery; will set up warfarin hold with enoxaparin bridge then.
3. HTN - at goal, no change.
4. DM2 - A1c, UACR today. Continue metformin. Eye exam due, he'll book with his optometrist.
5. CKD 3a - CMP today, keep off NSAIDs (he knows).
6. HLD - lipids.
7. Hx polyps - surveillance due ~2024.
8. Records requested from prior office.

RTC for preop mid-Sept.

documents.title: Your lab results
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Mr. Graves - your labs from Wednesday are back. INR is in your goal range, so stay on 5 mg nightly and we'll recheck at your pre-op visit. Sugar control (A1c) is good. Kidney function is at your usual stage 3 level, stable, and the urine protein test is normal. Cholesterol is well controlled on the atorvastatin. Blood counts normal. Nothing to change. See you in September.

Records received by fax from patient's previous primary care office, 46 pages, scanned to chart.

PCP summary of contents:
- Cardiac surgery summary 2013: mitral valve replaced with a mechanical prosthesis; warfarin started, INR goal 2.5-3.5, aspirin 81 added.
- Colonoscopy April 2021: polyps removed; repeat in 3 years recommended.
- Problem list: HTN, DM2, hyperlipidemia, CKD stage 3, chronic constipation, right hip osteoarthritis.
- Med list matches what he brought in.
- Labs 2019-2022: creatinine 1.2-1.4 range, A1c 6.6-7.1, INRs mostly in range.
- Immunizations: COVID primary series 2/2021 and booster 10/2021 (Pfizer), Tdap 2017, yearly flu shots. No pneumococcal or shingles vaccine on file.
- Routine screening there: hepatitis C not on file. AAA screening not on file.

reports.text: Sinus rhythm, rate in the 70s. Normal axis. Normal intervals. No ST or T wave changes. No prior tracing for comparison.

documents.title: Pre-operative Evaluation
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Preop eval for R THA 9/27 with his orthopedic surgeon.

No chest pain, no exertional SOB, no syncope. Functional capacity limited by the hip, not his heart - climbs a flight of stairs slowly, hip is the limiter. No bleeding problems. Takes his meds reliably.

Exam: regular rhythm, mechanical click crisp. Lungs clear. No edema. R hip antalgic.
ECG today NSR, normal.

Assessment: elevated-risk procedure in a patient with a mechanical MITRAL valve -> needs bridging. Cardiac risk otherwise acceptable; no further testing needed before surgery.

Anticoag plan (copy given to pt and faxed to surgeon):
- Last warfarin dose Wed 9/21 (hold 5 days).
- Start enoxaparin 80 mg SC q12h Fri 9/23. Last dose the morning of 9/26 (24 h before surgery).
- After surgery: warfarin back at 5 mg the evening of surgery if the surgeon agrees; enoxaparin restart when surgeon says hemostasis ok (usually 24-48 h), continue until INR >= 2.5.
- INR checks here after discharge.
- ASA 81: surgeon prefers to continue, fine.

CBC, BMP, INR today. Metformin hold morning of surgery. Cleared from medical standpoint.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - Right Total Hip Arthroplasty
documents.author: orthopedic surgery
documents.body:
REGIONAL HOSPITAL - ORTHOPEDIC SURGERY DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Admit 09/27/2022  Discharge 09/30/2022

Diagnosis: Severe primary osteoarthritis, right hip.
Procedure 09/27/2022: Right total hip arthroplasty, posterior approach. Uncomplicated.

Hospital course: Tolerated surgery well. Pain controlled with oral agents by POD1. Worked with PT, ambulating with walker POD1, stairs POD2. Warfarin resumed the evening of surgery at home dose; enoxaparin 80 mg q12h restarted POD1 per the anticoagulation plan from the patient's PCP. Incision clean, dry and intact at discharge. No fever. Mechanical valve sounds normal.

Allergies: NKDA.
Discharge meds: home medicines unchanged (warfarin 5 mg, lisinopril 20, metformin 1000 BID, atorvastatin 40, amlodipine 5, aspirin 81); enoxaparin 80 mg SC q12h until INR >= 2.5 per PCP.

Disposition: home with home PT. Posterior hip precautions.
Follow-up: orthopedics 2 weeks for wound check. PCP for INR within 1 week.

events.reason: INR check after hip surgery, on enoxaparin bridge

documents.title: INR Check
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Pt in for INR, 1 wk post R THA. Using walker. Incision covered, no drainage per pt. Taking warfarin 5 mg nightly and enoxaparin injections twice a day, no missed doses, no bleeding or bruising beyond the injection sites.

INR still below goal. Reviewed with PCP: continue warfarin 5 mg nightly, continue enoxaparin q12h. Recheck 1 week. Pt verbalized understanding, has enough syringes.

events.reason: INR check; flu and COVID vaccines

documents.title: INR Check and Immunizations
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
INR back in goal range today. Per PCP: stop enoxaparin, continue warfarin 5 mg nightly, next INR in 2 weeks then space out. Pt relieved to be done with the shots.

Flu vaccine (high-dose) L deltoid and COVID bivalent booster R deltoid given. Tolerated well, waited 15 min without issue. VIS given.

documents.title: Anticoagulation Follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
S: Here for routine warfarin follow-up for his mechanical mitral valve. Feels well, no complaints. Hip recovering nicely, off the walker, using a cane outdoors. Taking warfarin every evening, hasn't missed doses. No changes in what he eats, no new meds or supplements, no antibiotics. No bleeding, bruising, dark stools, chest pain or SOB.

O: BP 132/74, HR 78 regular. Click crisp. Lungs clear. R hip incision well healed.
INR today 2.6.

A/P: Mechanical MVR, INR 2.6 - in goal 2.5-3.5, at the low end but fine. Continue warfarin 5 mg nightly. Next INR in 4 weeks.
HTN fine.
Shingrix #1 today, #2 in 2-6 months.
RTC 3 months for diabetes visit.

documents.title: INR Result Call
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Called pt with today's INR. No missed doses, no bleeding, holiday plans don't involve big diet changes. Continue warfarin 5 mg nightly, recheck in 4 weeks. Pt agrees.
